resources.org: Government of Mauritius, as it reported to the United Nations
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, to report domestic violence.
resources.how: Call 139, free, any hour. In danger right now, call 999.

resources.name: Hotline 113 (child abuse)
resources.org: Government of Mauritius, as it reported to the United Nations
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, to report abuse of a child. You do not have to give your name.
resources.how: Call 113, free, any hour.

emergency.label: Police, fire and medical emergencies across the country

resources.name: Línea de la Vida
resources.org: Comisión Nacional de Salud Mental y Adicciones (CONASAMA)
resources.what: Mexico's free national line for emotional support, run by the health ministry. Trained professionals answer any hour about crisis, thoughts of suicide, violence, and alcohol or drug use.
resources.how: Call 800 911 2000 from any phone in Mexico. The line is in Spanish.

resources.name: Red Nacional de Refugios helpline
resources.what: A national network of shelters for women and their children escaping violence. Its helpline gives support and can help find a safe place to stay anywhere in Mexico.
resources.how: Call 800 822 4460. Shelter addresses are kept private for safety.

emergency.label: Emergency: free, any hour

resources.name: Helpline for domestic and sexual violence
resources.org: Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, listed by UNHCR
resources.what: The national helpline for anyone facing domestic or sexual violence.
resources.how: Call 0 8008 8008. In danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: Telefonul Copilului (child helpline)
resources.org: Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, listed by UNHCR
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, with psychological support and counselling for children, and help when a child needs protecting.
resources.how: Call 116 111, free, any hour.

emergency.label: Emergency response. You can also dial 103 for an ambulance, 102 for the police or 101 for the fire brigade

resources.name: 108 Child Helpline
resources.org: General Authority for Child and Family Development and Protection
resources.what: The national line for children: counselling and information, and fast help to protect a child at risk.
resources.how: Call 108.

emergency.label: All emergencies. Police: 122, ambulance: 124, fire: 123

resources.name: SOS line for women and children facing violence (SOS Nikšić)
resources.org: SOS telephone Nikšić, listed by UNHCR
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, for women and children facing violence.
resources.how: Call 080 111 111, free, any hour. In danger right now, call 112.
resources.chip: Line for women and children facing violence

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance or the fire service, call 15

resources.name: Help for women facing violence
resources.org: Ministry of Solidarity, Social Integration and Family
resources.what: More than 65 multifunctional centres for women across Morocco offer listening, support, social help and a way forward for women in difficulty, especially women facing violence. The ministry also runs a central unit for women victims of violence in Rabat.
resources.how: Ask the ministry's central unit for the centre nearest you: call 05 37 27 65 66. In danger right now, call the police on 19.

resources.name: Fonds d'entraide familiale (Family Mutual Aid Fund)
resources.what: When a court has ordered child support (nafaqa) but it is not being paid because the father cannot pay, is absent or cannot be found, this fund can pay an advance to a mother in need for her children, or to a wife in need. The law sets a ceiling of 350 dirhams a month for each person and 1,050 dirhams for a family.
resources.how: Apply to the president of the court of first instance that gave the judgment or where you live, with a copy of the judgment, the bailiff's report that it could not be enforced, your children's birth certificates and proof that you are in need (a medical assistance card or a certificate from the local authority). The court decides within 8 days.

resources.name: Aide sociale directe (direct social support)
resources.what: A monthly payment for families in need. From the end of November 2025 it is 250 dirhams for each of the first three children who are in school or under 6, 175 dirhams for a child not in school, and 375 dirhams for a child whose father has died. A family gets at least 500 dirhams a month.
resources.how: First register in the National Population Registry and the Unified Social Registry (RSU), then apply on the asd.ma portal. You get a decision within 30 days. Questions: call 05 20 19 60 60 or 05 20 19 40 70.

emergency.label: Police emergency, free, open 24 hours

resources.name: Gender-Based Violence Protection Units
resources.what: Police units in every region for people who have experienced gender-based violence, including rape and sexual assault.
resources.how: Go to the unit in your region. In Windhoek (Khomas), call 061 209 5375. In danger right now, call 10111.

resources.name: Maintenance Grant (child state grant)
resources.org: Ministry of Gender Equality and Child Welfare
resources.what: N$350 a month for each child under 18, for a parent on a low income whose spouse has died, has been in prison for six months or gets an old-age or disability grant, and for child-headed households. You must be a Namibian citizen or permanent resident.
resources.how: Apply in person at your constituency or regional office of the ministry, Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm. Bring the child's birth certificate, your ID, proof of income or a sworn statement that you are not working, your bank details and the other papers the ministry lists. Staff help you fill in the form.

emergency.label: Police control

resources.name: Khabar Garaun 1145
resources.what: The National Women Commission's helpline, open 24/7, where you can report violence against women and register a complaint.
resources.how: Call 1145. In danger right now, call the police on 100.

resources.name: Child Helpline Nepal 1098
resources.what: A toll-free line to report a child who is being abused, exploited, trafficked, at risk of child marriage, lost or in need of counselling. It can arrange rescue, counselling, medical referral, legal aid and family tracing.
resources.how: Call 1098.

resources.name: Safe Motherhood Programme (Aama)
resources.what: Giving birth at a public health facility is free: user fees for all delivery care were removed. You get cash for transport right after the birth (NPR 1,500 in mountain districts, NPR 1,000 in hill districts, NPR 500 in the Terai), and NPR 400 for completing four antenatal check-ups, at 4, 6, 8 and 9 months.
resources.how: Give birth at a public health facility with a birthing centre and bring a copy of your Nepali citizenship. Ask your nearest health post, primary health care centre, district hospital or district health office.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: Veilig Thuis
resources.what: The national advice and reporting centre for domestic violence and child abuse, whether it is happening to you or someone else. Free and open any hour.
resources.how: Call 0800-2000. You can also chat anonymously on weekdays from 9am to 5pm. In Dutch. In danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: 113 Zelfmoordpreventie
resources.what: Free, anonymous help by phone or chat, day and night, if you are thinking about suicide or worried about someone.
resources.how: Call 113 (or 0800-0113) from the Netherlands, or chat on the website. The website has a page in English.

resources.name: De Kindertelefoon
resources.what: For children and young people who want to talk about anything that is on their mind.
resources.how: Call 0800-0432 or chat, every day from 11am to 9pm. In Dutch.

resources.name: Kinderbijslag (child benefit)
resources.what: A regular payment towards the cost of raising your children.
resources.how: Register your baby's birth with your municipality. The SVB then sends you a letter within a few weeks, and you apply online in My SVB with DigiD or ask for a paper form. Register your baby with your health insurer within 4 months too.

resources.name: Kindgebonden budget
resources.what: An extra contribution towards the costs of children under 18, if you meet the conditions. With shared care, it goes to the parent who gets the kinderbijslag.
resources.how: If you qualify, you usually get a letter from the Dienst Toeslagen without having to apply. The full conditions are on toeslagen.nl.

resources.name: Free childhood vaccinations
resources.what: The vaccines in the national programme are free for children from birth to 18.
resources.how: Your child gets them at the consultatiebureau or the youth health service in your area.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: Women's Refuge crisis line
resources.what: Free information, advice and crisis help about family violence, any hour, from anywhere in New Zealand. Refuges run safe houses in every region.
resources.how: Call 0800 REFUGE. Do not let the person hurting you know you are thinking of leaving.

resources.name: 1737, Need to talk?
resources.what: Free call or text any hour to talk with a trained counsellor, or with a peer support worker, about feeling down, anxious or overwhelmed.
resources.how: Call or text 1737.

resources.name: PlunketLine
resources.what: Free parenting and child health advice from a registered nurse any hour, for children up to five. Free from mobiles too, and you do not need to be a Plunket client.
resources.how: Call any time. Ask for an interpreter if you need one. Breastfeeding and sleep video support can be booked through the line.

resources.name: Working for Families
resources.what: Payments to help with the cost of raising children 18 and under, based on family income. Best Start is part of it for babies.
resources.how: Check whether you qualify with the IRD calculator, then register in myIR or with the online form.

emergency.label: National Police emergency line, open day and night

resources.name: Casas Maternas (maternity waiting homes)
resources.what: A free place to stay near a hospital or health centre for pregnant women from communities far from one, usually from about 10 days before the due date, and after the birth. You are checked by health staff and learn about birth, breastfeeding and caring for your baby.
resources.how: Ask your midwife (partera), community health worker or nearest health unit, or go to the casa materna yourself.

emergency.label: National emergency number, free from any network

resources.name: WARIF 24-hour helpline
resources.what: A free, confidential 24-hour line for women and girls who have faced rape, sexual violence or trafficking, reaching callers across Nigeria.
resources.how: Call 0800 921 0009. Shelter addresses are kept private; ask the helpline if you need a safe place.

resources.name: She Writes Woman helpline
resources.what: A free mental health line answered at any hour by trained counsellors. Callers do not need airtime.

resources.name: Lagos State DSVA helpline
resources.org: Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency
resources.what: For people in Lagos State facing domestic violence, sexual assault or abuse. The agency coordinates legal, medical, emergency and counselling help.
resources.how: Call 0800 0333 333 any hour, or dial *6820# to report.

resources.name: Cece Yara Child Helpline
resources.what: A free 24-hour helpline for children and parents, run by staff trained to talk with children. It focuses on child sexual abuse and gives free legal, medical and therapy help.

emergency.label: Emergency services. Police: 192, ambulance: 194

resources.name: National free SOS mobile line (for women facing violence)
resources.org: National Council for Gender Equality, listed by UNFPA
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, for women facing gender-based or domestic violence. It is for mobile phones and works on every network.
resources.how: From a mobile phone, call 141 700, free, any hour. In danger right now, call 192 for the police or 112.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance or acute danger to life or health, call 113

resources.name: VO-linjen 116 006
resources.what: A free helpline, open 24/7, for anyone affected by domestic violence or abuse, and for their family, friends, colleagues and professionals. You can call anonymously.
resources.how: Call 116 006. In Norwegian and English.

resources.name: Mental Helse hjelpetelefonen
resources.what: A helpline, answered around the clock, where you can share anonymously and get support, advice and guidance.
resources.how: Call 116 123. You can also chat or send messages at sidetmedord.no.

resources.name: Kirkens SOS
resources.what: Someone to talk to, around the clock every day, holidays too. You can remain anonymous.
resources.how: Call 22 40 00 40, chat at soschat.no, or send a message.

resources.name: 116 111 crisis line for children and young people
resources.org: Crisis hotline for children and young people
resources.what: A free emergency line for children and teenagers who are victims of violence, abuse or neglect.

resources.name: Helsestasjon (child health centre)
resources.what: A free service with health checks, childhood vaccines, parenting advice and extra follow-up for children aged 0 to 5. Pregnant women get check-ups, and a midwife or health nurse visits new mothers and babies at home after the birth.
resources.how: Contact the helsestasjon where you live. An interpreter is used when needed.

resources.name: Barnetrygd (child benefit)
resources.what: 2,012 kroner a month for each child under 18, from February 2026. Families in Finnmark, Svalbard and some Nord-Troms municipalities get 512 kroner a month more.
resources.how: For a child born in Norway it is usually paid to the mother automatically. You must apply in some cases, such as when the child was born abroad.

emergency.label: Emergency

resources.name: Child protection hotline 1100
resources.what: The national child protection hotline, for a child at risk of violence or neglect.
resources.how: Call 1100. If a child is in danger right now, call 9999.

emergency.label: Ambulance and rescue. Police, dial 15. Fire, dial 16

resources.name: Helpline 1099
resources.what: A free government helpline for legal advice and help when your rights are violated. Most complaints it handles are about women's rights, and it can refer you to the right office.
resources.how: Dial 1099. You can also send a WhatsApp to 0333 9085709.

resources.name: Rozan Counseling Helpline
resources.what: Counselling by phone for emotional and mental health struggles, including violence against women and child sexual abuse.
resources.how: Call 0304 111 1741, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Benazir Nashonuma
resources.org: Ministry of Poverty Alleviation and Social Safety
resources.what: Cash every three months for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers and children under two in families on the Benazir Income Support Programme: PKR 2,000 for each mother and boy, and PKR 2,500 for each girl, with special nutritious food.
resources.how: It is for families already on the Benazir Income Support Programme. Mothers go to regular check-ups and keep their children's vaccines up to date.

emergency.label: The national emergency number, free from anywhere in the country, for when a life is in danger

resources.name: Línea 182
resources.org: Instituto Nacional de la Mujer (INAMU), listed by the Ministerio Público
resources.what: A line for women facing violence, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for information and advice. The Ministerio Público also has a free legal aid office for victims of crime, and its regional offices take reports any hour.
resources.how: Call 182. In danger right now, call 911, or the Policía Nacional on 104.

emergency.label: The national emergency system, free from any phone

resources.name: Línea 137 SOS Mujer
resources.org: Ministerio de la Mujer (Ministry of Women)
resources.what: A free line, open 24 hours across the country, for women facing violence. It gives psychological support and legal and social guidance, and can guide you through making a report.
resources.how: Call 137 from a landline or any mobile. In danger right now, call 911.

emergency.label: Police. For fire, call 116; for an ambulance (SAMU), call 106

resources.name: Línea 100
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations (MIMP)
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day of the year, for anyone facing violence against women or family members, or who knows of a case. A team gives legal, psychological and social advice.
resources.how: Call 100 from a landline or mobile anywhere in Peru. Help is in Spanish, Quechua and Aymara. In danger right now, call 105.

resources.name: Línea 113, option 5
resources.what: Free, confidential help from psychologists, any hour, for an emotional crisis or when you feel at risk.
resources.how: Call 113 and choose option 5, or write on WhatsApp to 955 557 000. In Spanish.

resources.name: Juntos
resources.org: Ministry of Development and Social Inclusion (MIDIS)
resources.what: Money every two months for families in poverty with a pregnant woman, children or young people up to 19, as long as they keep up prenatal check-ups, child health checks and school.
resources.how: Families are chosen and signed up by MIDIS through its local staff.

emergency.label: Police, fire, medical and rescue

resources.name: NCMH Crisis Hotline
resources.what: The government's mental health crisis line, open any hour, for anyone in emotional distress or thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Dial 1553 toll-free from a landline. From a mobile, call 0919 057 1553 (Smart/TNT) or 0917 899 8727 (Globe/TM).

resources.name: Solo Parent ID
resources.org: City or Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office
resources.what: Under the Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act, a solo parent can get an ID that unlocks benefits such as leave, discounts and priority for some programs.
resources.how: Apply at your city or municipal social welfare office (or Solo Parent Office). The ID is renewed every year.

emergency.label: Any emergency. For an ambulance you can also call 999

resources.name: Niebieska Linia
resources.what: A free line, open around the clock, for people facing violence at home and for anyone who sees it happening.
resources.how: Call 800 120 002. In Polish.

resources.name: 116 123 emotional support line
resources.org: National helpline for people in emotional crisis
resources.what: A support line, open around the clock, for adults going through an emotional crisis.
resources.how: Call 116 123. In Polish.

resources.name: Centrum Wsparcia
resources.what: Free support, around the clock, for adults in a mental health crisis.
resources.how: Call 800 70 2222. In Polish.

resources.name: 116 111 helpline for children and young people
resources.org: Telefon Zaufania dla Dzieci i Młodzieży
resources.what: Free, anonymous support for children and teenagers.

resources.name: Rodzina 800+
resources.what: 800 zł a month for every child until they turn 18, whatever the family's income.
resources.how: Apply online to ZUS through PUE ZUS or the mZUS app, the Emp@tia portal, or your online bank. Apply within 3 months of your baby's birth to be paid from the day of birth.

emergency.label: Any emergency, free, any hour, every day

resources.name: Serviço de Informação às Vítimas de Violência Doméstica
resources.org: Comissão para a Cidadania e a Igualdade de Género (CIG)
resources.what: A free, anonymous and confidential information line for victims of domestic violence, open 24 hours a day, every day of the year.
resources.how: Call 800 202 148, or send a free, confidential text message to 3060. In danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: SNS suicide prevention line 1411
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day of the year. Psychologists and nurses who specialise in mental health answer if you are thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call 1411.

resources.name: Linha de Apoio à Criança 116 111
resources.org: Child support line, listed by the Government of Portugal
resources.what: A free line, open 24 hours a day, every day, where children can get support about things that affect them directly.
resources.how: Call 116 111. If a child is missing, call 116 000, also free and open any hour.

resources.name: SNS 24 and its psychological counselling line
resources.what: The national health line, with clinical help any hour of the day. It includes a psychological counselling service, in Portuguese and in English.
resources.how: Call 808 24 24 24. Calls cost the same as a call to a landline.

resources.name: Abono de família pré-natal (pregnancy allowance)
resources.what: A monthly payment for pregnant women from the 13th week of pregnancy, for households under an income limit. Mothers who live alone or only with their children get 35% more.
resources.how: Apply online through Segurança Social Direta, in person at a Segurança Social office or at a Loja do Cidadão. Online, you only need to allow your pregnancy certificate to be shared through SNS 24.

resources.name: Abono de família para crianças e jovens (child benefit)
resources.what: A monthly payment to help with the cost of raising children, until they finish compulsory schooling. The amount depends on household income, the child's age and how many children get it. Single-parent families can get more.
resources.how: Apply online through Segurança Social Direta or in person at a Segurança Social office. Apply within 6 months of the birth and it is paid from the month after the baby was born.

emergency.label: Emergency, including an ambulance

resources.name: National Mental Health Helpline
resources.org: Ministry of Public Health and Hamad Medical Corporation
resources.what: Free, confidential support from mental health professionals, who speak a range of languages.
resources.how: Call 16000, 8am to 7pm Sunday to Thursday and 8am to 3pm on Saturday. In a crisis, call 999.

resources.name: Antenatal care at PHCC health centres
resources.what: Pregnancy care at every PHCC health centre, for citizens and residents registered there: a first visit as soon as the pregnancy is confirmed, with tests and scans, then check-ups up to 34 weeks, when you are referred to hospital.
resources.how: Call 107 or walk in to your health centre to book.

resources.name: Postnatal care at PHCC health centres
resources.org: Primary Health Care Corporation (PHCC), with Hamad Medical Corporation
resources.what: A check on your body and your feelings after the birth, with advice and counselling. A maternal and child health counsellor calls you within 3 to 5 working days of the request.
resources.how: Call 107, or ask the hospital where you gave birth or your health centre doctor to refer you.

emergency.label: The European emergency number, free from a landline or mobile

resources.name: Linia telefonică 0800 500 333
resources.org: Agenția Națională pentru Egalitatea de Șanse între Femei și Bărbați (ANES)
resources.what: A free national line, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for domestic violence, human trafficking and discrimination based on sex. It gives immediate guidance, basic legal and psychological counselling, referrals to local services and information on getting a protection order. Victims, family, neighbours and witnesses can call, and you can stay anonymous.
resources.how: Call 0800 500 333, free from any national network. In danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: Telefonul Copilului 116 111
resources.what: The national helpline for children and teenagers, free: for abuse, psychological counselling and any other problem involving a child. You do not have to say who you are.
resources.how: Call 116 111, Monday to Friday, 10am to 8pm, from Orange, Telekom or Vodafone landlines and mobiles.

resources.name: Ordin de protecție (protection order)
resources.org: Agenția Națională pentru Egalitatea de Șanse între Femei și Bărbați (ANES)
resources.what: ANES offers a model application for a protection order against an abuser, with advice on filling it in, and the forms to ask the state for free legal help (ajutor public judiciar).
resources.how: Download the forms from ANES's page for victims. For help with them, call 0800 500 333.

emergency.label: Emergency. For an ambulance, call 912

resources.name: Gender-based violence line 3512
resources.org: Rwanda National Police and Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB)
resources.what: A toll-free short code for reporting domestic violence and gender-based violence.
resources.how: Call 3512. In danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: Isange One Stop Centres
resources.what: Centres, based in hospitals across the country, that give free medical, legal and psychosocial help to survivors of gender-based violence and child abuse, all in one place.
resources.how: Call Isange on 3029, or go to the Isange centre at your district hospital.

resources.name: Child Help Line 116
resources.org: Rwanda National Police and Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB)
resources.what: A toll-free short code for reporting child abuse, answered at the Rwanda National Police call centre.
resources.how: Call 116.

resources.name: Health line 114
resources.org: Rwanda Health Communication Centre, Rwanda Biomedical Centre (RBC)
resources.what: A free health call centre, open Monday to Saturday, where specialists give health information and counselling and help you find health services.
resources.how: Call 114.

emergency.label: Ministry of Interior emergency and security reports. Police: 999; Saudi Red Crescent ambulance: 997; Civil Defense: 998

resources.name: Domestic Violence Reporting Center 1919
resources.org: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD)
resources.what: A free, confidential line, open any hour, for anyone being abused at home or who knows someone who is. Citizens and residents can call, in Arabic or English.
resources.how: Call 1919, email 1919@hrsd.gov.sa, or report through the ministry's app. In danger right now, call 911.

resources.name: 937 health line
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's line, open any hour, where doctors give medical advice by phone, including advice on poisoning, and take questions about health services.
resources.how: Call 937. For an emergency, call 997 for an ambulance.

resources.name: Citizen Account Program
resources.org: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD)
resources.what: Cash support paid directly to eligible Saudi households, to protect families from the effects of economic reforms. You register yourself and your dependents.
resources.how: Register free on the Citizen Account e-portal or app (in Arabic and English): fill in your and your dependents' details, attach the documents and submit. Questions: call 19912.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance, dial 194; for the fire service, dial 193

resources.name: Ambulance 194
resources.what: The number for an ambulance. Serbia has separate numbers for the police (192), the fire service (193) and an ambulance (194). The police number is also a free call for reporting any kind of violence, including at home, and you may call without giving your name.
resources.how: Call 194 for an ambulance, or 192 for the police.

resources.name: НАДЕЛ, Национална дечја линија (National Children's Line)
resources.what: A counselling line for children and young people, open 24 hours a day, every day of the year. Chat is open every day from 6pm to 10pm.

resources.name: Free support lines of the Dr Laza Lazarević Clinic
resources.org: Dr Laza Lazarević Clinic for Psychiatric Disorders
resources.what: Free lines open 24 hours a day, every day: option 1 for suicide prevention, option 3 for teenagers, option 4 for psychological support for women before, during and after pregnancy, and option 5 for parents and carers of children on the autism spectrum.
resources.how: Call 0800 309 309 and choose the option you need.

resources.name: Родитељски додатак (parental allowance)
resources.org: Municipalities, through the government's eBeba service
resources.what: A payment from the state when a child is born.
resources.how: You can apply for it in the maternity hospital, through the eBeba (“Bebo, dobro došla na svet”) service, when the birth is registered there. The request goes to the municipality where you live.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance or the fire service, dial 995

resources.name: National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline (NAVH)
resources.org: Ministry of Social and Family Development
resources.what: A line open any hour to get help with, or report, family violence, abuse, neglect, sexual violence or sexual harassment. Victims, family, neighbours and professionals can all call.
resources.how: Call 1800-777-0000, or use the online report form. Airtime charges apply from a mobile.

resources.name: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS)
resources.what: Someone to talk to, any hour, if you are in crisis or having thoughts of suicide.
resources.how: Call 1767, or send a WhatsApp to CareText on 9151 1767. Both are open 24 hours. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: ComCare
resources.org: Ministry of Social and Family Development
resources.what: Money help for families on a low income or in urgent need, from short-term help with living costs to help right away.
resources.how: Call the ComCare Hotline, open 7am to midnight every day, or visit a Social Service Office. For Singapore Citizens, and Permanent Residents living with a family member who is a citizen. Airtime charges apply from a mobile.

resources.name: Baby Bonus
resources.org: Ministry of Social and Family Development
resources.what: For each child who is a Singapore Citizen: a Cash Gift of $11,000 or more, paid in steps until age 6½, and a $5,000 grant into a Child Development Account, which the government also matches when you save. Parents must be married for the Cash Gift.
resources.how: Apply in the LifeSG app when you register the birth.

resources.name: Legal Aid Bureau
resources.what: Legal help with civil cases, including divorce, for people with limited means and a reasonable case. You can see a duty lawyer for advice.
resources.how: Register on the Legal Aid Bureau's applicant portal, then book an appointment before you go. Open weekdays, 8:30am to 5pm.

emergency.label: Emergency. You can also dial 155 for an ambulance, 158 for the police or 150 for the fire service

resources.name: Národná linka pre ženy zažívajúce násilie (national line for women experiencing violence)
resources.org: Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family, run by the Institute for Labour and Family Research
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, for women experiencing violence.
resources.how: Call 0800 212 212, free. In danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: Príspevok pri narodení dieťaťa (birth allowance)
resources.org: Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family, and the Offices of Labour, Social Affairs and Family
resources.what: A one-off payment to the mother after a birth: €829.86 for a child from a first to fourth birth, and €151.37 from a fifth birth on, with more for twins or more. It is lost if you did not go to monthly gynaecology check-ups from the fourth month of pregnancy, or did not register the baby with a children's doctor.
resources.how: For a baby born in Slovakia you do not need to apply: it is paid by itself once the birth is registered. Tell your local Office of Labour, Social Affairs and Family which bank account to pay. For a baby born abroad, take an officially translated birth certificate to the office. The claim runs out 12 months after the birth.

resources.name: Prídavok na dieťa (child allowance)
resources.org: Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family, and the Offices of Labour, Social Affairs and Family
resources.what: A monthly payment to a parent raising a dependent child, paid up to age 25 while the child is still dependent. The ministry gives €60 a month, with €110 more in the month a child starts first grade.
resources.how: Apply in writing, or online with a qualified electronic signature, at the Office of Labour, Social Affairs and Family where you live. You can claim it for up to six months back.

emergency.label: Emergency: ambulance, fire service and rescue. You can also dial 113 for the police

resources.name: SOS telefon (line for anyone facing violence)
resources.org: Društvo SOS telefon, listed by the Government of Slovenia
resources.what: A free line, open day and night all year, for anyone who needs help or information about any kind of violence.
resources.how: Call 080 11 55, free, any hour. In danger right now, call 113 or 112.

resources.name: TOM telefon (line for children and teenagers)
resources.org: Listed by the Government of Slovenia
resources.what: A free, anonymous and confidential line for children and teenagers.
resources.how: Call 116 111, free.

resources.name: Pomoč ob rojstvu otroka (birth grant)
resources.org: Ministry for Demography, Family and Social Affairs, through the social work centres
resources.what: A one-off payment of €441.60 (from March 1, 2026) for each newborn, to buy what the baby needs, where a parent lives in Slovenia.
resources.how: The mother applies on e-uprava or at the social work centre (center za socialno delo) where she lives, from 60 days before the due date to 60 days after the birth.

resources.name: Otroški dodatek (child allowance)
resources.org: Ministry for Demography, Family and Social Affairs, through the social work centres
resources.what: A monthly payment for each child under 18, set by the family's income: from about €25.70 to €177.24 a child, a little more for second and later children, and 30% more for a single parent.
resources.how: Apply on e-uprava or at the social work centre (CSD) where you live. Questions: 01 369 75 00.

emergency.label: Police. From a cellphone, 112. Ambulance, 10177

resources.name: GBV Command Centre
resources.what: A 24-hour line staffed by social workers who give counselling and support to people facing gender-based violence, and can send a local social worker.
resources.how: Call toll-free, or dial *120*7867# from any cellphone to have them call you back.

resources.name: Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.org: South African Depression and Anxiety Group
resources.what: A toll-free crisis line, open any hour, for anyone thinking about suicide or worried about someone.
resources.how: Call toll-free from any network.

resources.name: Childline South Africa
resources.what: A free helpline any hour for children, and for adults worried about a child.
resources.how: Dial 116, free from all networks.

resources.name: Child Support Grant
resources.what: A monthly grant for the primary caregiver of a child under 18 in a low-income household.
resources.how: Apply free at your nearest SASSA office. Bring your ID and the child's birth certificate.

emergency.label: Police, with interpreters at set hours. For fire and rescue, call 119

resources.name: 여성긴급전화 1366 (Women's Emergency Line)
resources.org: Ministry of Gender Equality and Family
resources.what: Emergency counselling, protection and shelter referrals, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, for women facing domestic violence, sexual violence, prostitution, dating violence or stalking, and for their families and neighbours.
resources.how: Call 1366, with no area code. Migrant women are put through to the 이주여성1366 line for counselling in their own language.

resources.name: Danuri Call Center 1577-1366
resources.org: Hotline for migrant women and multicultural families
resources.what: Phone counselling 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, in 13 languages, including emergency shelter and referrals for domestic violence, sexual violence and trafficking.
resources.how: Call 1577-1366. Languages: Vietnamese, Chinese, English, Japanese, Filipino, Tagalog, Russian, Mongolian, Thai, Khmer, Uzbek, Lao and Nepali.

resources.name: 자살예방 상담전화 109 (suicide prevention line)
resources.what: The national suicide prevention line, with counsellors on duty 24 hours a day.
resources.how: Call 109, with no area code.

resources.name: 부모급여 (parent allowance)
resources.what: ₩1,000,000 a month for a baby under 1 and ₩500,000 a month at age 1, in 2026. If your child goes to daycare, the government pays the gap between the allowance and the daycare fee.
resources.how: Apply at your local community service centre (you can do it when you register the birth), or online through Bokjiro or Gov24. Apply within 60 days of the birth and it is paid from the birth month. For questions, call the Ministry of Health and Welfare on 129.

resources.name: Korea Legal Aid Corporation 132
resources.what: The national legal aid line.
resources.how: Call 132.

emergency.label: Any emergency, free from any phone, even with no credit or signal

resources.what: Free, confidential help any hour for women facing any form of violence, and for the people around them.
resources.how: Call 016, or send a WhatsApp message (no calls) to 600 000 016. The phone line works in 53 languages. You can also email 016-online@igualdad.gob.es.

resources.name: 024 suicide prevention line
resources.what: Free, confidential and open every hour of the year, for anyone with thoughts of suicide and for their family and friends.
resources.how: Call 024 from anywhere in Spain. There is also a chat run by the Red Cross and a sign language video service. If a life is in danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: ANAR helpline
resources.what: Free, confidential help for children and teenagers, any hour.
resources.how: Call 900 20 20 10 or open the chat on the website. In Spanish, with phone interpreting for other languages.

resources.name: Ingreso Mínimo Vital
resources.what: A monthly payment for people and families who do not have enough to cover the basics. Families on it with children also get a child supplement.
resources.how: Apply online at imv.seg-social.es and keep the reference code you are given. For information, call 020. In the Basque Country apply through Lanbide; in Navarra and Catalonia, through local offices.

emergency.label: Police emergency, for anything that needs the police right away

resources.name: 1938 Women Help Line
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Child Affairs
resources.what: A toll-free helpline for women, open 24 hours every day in all three of the country's languages. It takes complaints of violence, gives counselling and legal advice, follows up, and refers you to other services.
resources.how: Call 1938. In danger right now, call the police on 119.

resources.name: 1926 National Mental Health Helpline
resources.what: The national mental health helpline, for anything you want to talk about regarding your mental health. You can call from any network.
resources.how: Call 1926.

resources.name: 1929 ChildLine
resources.what: A free, confidential line, open any hour, every day, for any child or adult to report child abuse or ask about a child. It also connects children with longer-term care. In Sinhala, Tamil and English.
resources.how: Call 1929 free from any network.

emergency.label: Ambulance, police and rescue services

resources.name: Kvinnofridslinjen
resources.org: Nationellt centrum för kvinnofrid (NCK), Uppsala University
resources.what: A free national support line for women subjected to violence, open 24 hours a day. You can stay anonymous.
resources.how: Call 116 016, or the old number 020-50 50 50. You can also chat in Swedish on the website: Monday and Thursday 3pm to 9pm, Sunday 11am to 5pm.

resources.name: Mind Självmordslinjen
resources.what: For anyone having thoughts of suicide, or worried about someone who is. Open 24 hours a day, every day, and all calls are anonymous.
resources.how: Call 90101 or chat on the website. In Swedish and English.

resources.name: Bris
resources.what: For children and young people under 18, and anyone worried about someone that age. Open 24 hours a day.
resources.how: Call or text 116 111, or chat on the website. In Swedish and English.

resources.name: 1177 healthcare advice
resources.what: Medical advice any hour of the day, and where to find the nearest psychiatric emergency unit.
resources.how: Call 1177. In Swedish and English.

resources.name: Midwife clinic (barnmorskemottagning)
resources.what: Free visits during pregnancy to see how you and the baby are doing, with advice and help getting ready for the birth.
resources.how: Contact a midwife clinic yourself as soon as you know you are pregnant. If you don't speak Swedish, say you need an interpreter when you book.

resources.name: Barnbidrag (child allowance)
resources.what: 1,250 kronor a month for each child, paid automatically to parents who live in Sweden, until the child turns 16. Families with two or more children also get a large-family supplement (flerbarnstillägg).
resources.how: You do not need to apply. With joint custody it is split between the guardians. Tell Försäkringskassan about changes that could affect it.

emergency.label: Works with a foreign SIM too. Also 117 for the police, 144 for an ambulance, 118 for the fire service

resources.name: Opferhilfe 142
resources.what: A free, confidential national line for people who have experienced physical, psychological or sexual violence, and for their relatives. Open around the clock since May 2026. Trained specialists support you and refer you on.
resources.how: Call 142. You can stay anonymous.

resources.name: Die Dargebotene Hand / La Main Tendue / Telefono Amico
resources.what: Someone to talk to, around the clock, for adults. Also by email and chat.
resources.how: Call 143. A call costs CHF 0.20 to 0.70. In German, French or Italian.

resources.name: 147 Pro Juventute
resources.what: For children and young people, around the clock. Also by WhatsApp, email and peer chat.
resources.how: Call 147.

resources.name: Pro Juventute Elternberatung
resources.what: Free, confidential advice for parents, 24/7, on parenting, child development, family life and times of acute stress.
resources.how: Call 058 261 61 61. The Elternnotruf on 0848 354 555 also gives free, confidential help when parenting feels overwhelming.

resources.name: Familienzulagen (family allowances)
resources.what: 215 francs a month per child from birth to 16, and 268 francs a month for children in education aged 15 to 25. Cantons and employers can pay more, and some pay a special allowance at birth.
resources.how: It is not paid automatically. Employees apply through their employer; self-employed people apply to their family compensation fund; people not in work apply to the cantonal fund. You can claim up to five years back.

emergency.label: Police. For fire or emergency rescue, call 119

resources.name: 113 Protection Hotline
resources.what: A hotline open 24 hours a day, every day of the year, for advice and reports about domestic violence, sexual assault, sexual harassment, and the protection of children, young people, older people and people with disabilities.
resources.how: Call 113. Interpreters are available in English, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Thai, Cambodian and Japanese. In danger right now, call the police on 110.

resources.name: 1925 安心專線 (Peace of Mind Line)
resources.what: Free psychological counselling by phone, 24 hours a day, every day of the year. It responds to suicide crises and contacts the police for an emergency rescue when needed.
resources.how: Call 1925.

resources.name: Subsidised prenatal check-ups
resources.org: Health Promotion Administration, Ministry of Health and Welfare
resources.what: 14 government-paid prenatal check-ups, 3 ultrasound scans (early, middle and late pregnancy), tests for anaemia and gestational diabetes at 24 to 28 weeks, a Group B strep test at 35 to 37 weeks, and 2 prenatal health education sessions.
resources.how: No application is needed. Take your Mommy Health Handbook (孕媽咪健康手冊) and your National Health Insurance card to a contracted clinic.

resources.name: 育兒津貼 (childcare allowance for children under 2)
resources.org: Social and Family Affairs Administration, Ministry of Health and Welfare
resources.what: A monthly allowance for a child under 2 who is a Taiwanese national and is not in public or quasi-public childcare: NT$5,000 a month for a first child, NT$6,000 for a second and NT$7,000 for a third or later child.
resources.how: Apply online on the Social and Family Affairs Administration's website (with a card reader and your citizen certificate or NHI card), or at the township, city or district office where your child is registered, with ID, your household record and a copy of your bank account book.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: National Child Helpline 116
resources.org: C-Sema, with the Government of Tanzania
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, for children and for women and girls at risk of violence. Parents, family and neighbours can call to report a child in danger.
resources.how: Dial 116 from any phone.

resources.name: Afya Call Center
resources.what: Free health advice any hour from doctors and nurses, including mental health and sexual and reproductive health, and help finding a health facility near you.
resources.how: Dial 199.

emergency.label: Emergency report. For medical emergencies (Narenthorn EMS Center), call 1669; for fire, 199

resources.name: สายด่วน 1300 (Social Assistance Center hotline)
resources.org: Ministry of Social Development and Human Security
resources.what: The ministry's centre for advice and complaints for anyone facing social problems, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, in every area.
resources.how: Call 1300. In danger right now, call 191.

resources.name: สายด่วนสุขภาพจิต 1323 (mental health hotline)
resources.what: A mental health hotline open 24 hours a day, if you cannot sleep, feel panicked or are worried.
resources.how: Call 1323.

resources.name: เงินอุดหนุนเพื่อการเลี้ยงดูเด็กแรกเกิด (child support grant)
resources.org: Ministry of Social Development and Human Security
resources.what: 600 baht a month for each child until age 6, for households whose members earn on average no more than 100,000 baht a person a year.
resources.how: Ask your provincial Office of Social Development and Human Security how to register.

emergency.label: Police. Fire, 990. Ambulance, 811

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline (800-SAVE)
resources.what: A line open any hour to get help with domestic or gender-based violence. It offers crisis help and counselling, and can arrange a place at the national shelter for women and their children.
resources.how: Dial 800-SAVE (800-7283). Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Lifeline
resources.what: Free, anonymous support any hour for anyone in emotional crisis or thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call 800-5588 or 866-5433. Both are toll-free.

resources.name: Children's Authority hotline
resources.org: Children's Authority of Trinidad and Tobago
resources.what: The government agency that protects children. Call any hour to report a child you think is being abused or neglected.
resources.how: Dial 996 or 800-2014. Children who want to talk to someone can call Childline on 800-4321 or 131. Normal call charges may apply.

emergency.label: Police in towns. Ambulance: 190, fire: 198, National Guard in the countryside: 193

resources.name: Ligne verte 1899 (line for women facing violence)
resources.org: Ministry of Women, Family, Children and Seniors, listed by UN Women
resources.what: The national line for women who have faced violence.
resources.how: Call 1899. In danger right now, call 197 for the police.

emergency.label: Emergency Call Centre (Acil Çağrı Merkezi), when you are in immediate danger

resources.name: ALO 183
resources.org: Ministry of Family and Social Services (Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı)
resources.what: A free line, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for help with violence and with services for families, women, children, disabled and older people, and veterans and their relatives. Staff who speak Kurdish and Arabic answer calls in those languages.
resources.how: Call 183, free from within Turkey. Deaf callers can send a free SMS to 183 with their name, ID number and request, or make a sign-language video call on 0 549 381 0 183 (weekdays 8am to midnight, Saturdays 8am to 5pm). From abroad, call +90 312 253 92 00.

resources.name: Protection under Law 6284
resources.org: Ministry of Family and Social Services
resources.what: Under Law 6284 a judge can order an abuser to stop threatening or contacting you, to leave your shared home and stay away from it and from your children's school and your workplace, and to hand over weapons. A first order lasts up to six months, and the procedures cost nothing. ŞÖNİM violence prevention centres, open any hour, give psychological, legal and social guidance, and if you cannot afford a lawyer the local bar association (baro) assigns one free.
resources.how: Ask at the governor's or district governor's office, a police or gendarmerie station, the public prosecutor's office or a family court. You can also report violence with the KADES app. ALO 183 can tell you how to reach a ŞÖNİM.

resources.name: Doğum yardımı (birth support)
resources.org: Ministry of Family and Social Services
resources.what: For children born alive on or after 1 January 2025 to a Turkish-citizen mother or father: a one-off 5,000 TL for a first child; 1,500 TL a month for a second child and 5,000 TL a month for a third or later child, until the child turns 5.
resources.how: Apply on e-Devlet with your own account, by the time a first child is 12 months old, or 60 months for later children. Without e-Devlet, the ministry's provincial offices or social service centres (SHM) can help. Payments are made through Halkbank.

emergency.label: National emergency number. 112 works too

resources.name: Sauti 116
resources.org: Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, to report abuse of a child or violence against a woman. Social workers and psychologists answer and pass cases on for help.
resources.how: Dial 116 from any phone. You can also text 116.

resources.name: MIFUMI domestic violence helpline
resources.what: A free line, open any hour, for women and children facing violence at home. Counsellors help you make a safety plan and can help with legal advice and emergency shelter.
resources.how: Call 0800 200 250. It is toll-free in Uganda.

resources.name: Mental Health Uganda toll-free line
resources.what: Free, confidential support with your mental health, on a weekday.
resources.how: Call 0800 21 21 21, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm.

emergency.label: Police

resources.name: Government hotline 15-47
resources.org: Ministry of Social Policy, Family and Unity of Ukraine
resources.what: The government's free, confidential hotline, open any hour, for people who have suffered or witnessed domestic violence, gender-based violence, violence against children or human trafficking. Specialists give information, psychological support and legal advice.
resources.how: Call 15-47. In danger right now, call the police on 102.

resources.name: National hotline on domestic violence, human trafficking and gender discrimination
resources.org: La Strada-Ukraine, listed by the Ministry of Social Policy
resources.what: A free national line, open any hour, for people facing domestic violence, human trafficking or gender discrimination.
resources.how: Call 116 123 free from a mobile, or 0 800 500 335 free from a landline.

resources.name: National hotline for children and youth
resources.org: La Strada-Ukraine, listed by the Ministry of Social Policy
resources.what: A national line for children and young people, open every day from 9am to 9pm.
resources.how: Call 116 111 free from a mobile, or 0 800 500 225 from a landline.

resources.name: Free legal aid hotline
resources.org: Free legal aid system, listed by the Ministry of Social Policy
resources.what: The free hotline of Ukraine's state free legal aid system, listed by the Ministry of Social Policy for people who have suffered violence.
resources.how: Call 0 800 213 103. The call is free.

resources.name: єМалятко (eMalyatko) and the birth payment
resources.org: Diia, with the Pension Fund of Ukraine
resources.what: One free application that registers your baby's birth and can also claim the birth payment and the baby package. For a child born from 1 January 2026, the birth payment is 50,000 hryvnias in one sum. If you did not get a baby package (пакунок малюка) at the hospital, you can take 8,451 hryvnias instead.
resources.how: Apply within 30 days of the birth on the Diia portal, or at the maternity hospital, a civil registry office (ДРАЦС) or an administrative service centre (ЦНАП). If your child already has a birth certificate, claim the birth payment at the Pension Fund.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance, call 998; for the fire department (Civil Defence), 997

resources.name: DFWAC helpline 800111
resources.org: Dubai Foundation for Women and Children
resources.what: A free helpline, open 24/7, for women and children facing violence: urgent help, consultations and information about the foundation's services.
resources.how: Call 800111, message 800111 on WhatsApp, or email help@dfwac.ae. In danger right now, call 999.

resources.name: Child protection hotline 116111
resources.what: The Ministry of Interior's hotline for reporting child abuse.
resources.how: Call 116111. You can also report through the Ministry of Interior Child Protection Centre's website or the Hemayati app.

resources.name: EWAA Shelters for Women and Children
resources.org: EWAA Shelters for Women and Children
resources.what: The hotline of EWAA's shelters for women and children, listed by the UAE government for abuse and for human trafficking.

resources.name: Maternity leave in the private sector
resources.what: Women working in the private sector get 60 days of maternity leave: 45 days on full pay and 15 on half pay. Up to 45 more days without pay are allowed for an illness caused by the pregnancy or birth, with a medical certificate. Back at work, you get one or two paid nursing breaks a day, an hour at most in all, for six months after the birth.
resources.how: Tell your employer. Article 30 of the UAE Labour Law has more on maternity.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: National Domestic Abuse Helpline
resources.what: Free, confidential support any hour, every day of the year, from trained women advisers, in many languages. They can help with safety planning and finding a refuge.
resources.how: Call any time, or use the live chat on the helpline's website.

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.what: Someone to talk to, free, any time of day or night, from any phone. You do not have to be suicidal to call.

resources.name: PANDAS Foundation helpline
resources.what: Free support for parents struggling with their mental health in pregnancy and after birth, and for the people around them.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday, 10am to 5pm, or book a call back on the website.

resources.name: National Breastfeeding Helpline
resources.org: Breastfeeding Network and Association of Breastfeeding Mothers
resources.what: Breastfeeding support any hour, every day, from trained volunteers who have breastfed. Help in Welsh and Polish is on the same number.
resources.how: Call any time. Calls cost the same as a call to a number starting 01 or 02.

resources.name: Gingerbread Single Parent Helpline
resources.what: Free advice for single parents in England and Wales on money, benefits, child maintenance, work, housing and separation.
resources.how: Call or use the webchat on the website. In Scotland, One Parent Families Scotland runs the Lone Parent Helpline on 0808 801 0323.

resources.name: Child Benefit
resources.what: A regular payment for each child you are responsible for. Only one person can claim for a child.
resources.how: Claim online or in the HMRC app from 48 hours after you register the birth. A claim can be backdated up to 3 months.

emergency.label: Police. For a medical emergency, call 105

resources.name: Servicio telefónico 0800 4141
resources.what: A free, confidential national line, open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, for women over 18 living in Uruguay who face domestic violence. It listens, advises and helps you find a way forward. Relatives and others who know about a case can call too.
resources.how: Call 0800 4141 or *4141. Deaf women can make a video call on 092 626 928, Monday to Friday, 9am to 2pm. In danger right now, call 911.

resources.name: Línea de Vida 0800 0767
resources.org: Suicide prevention line, listed by the Ministerio de Salud Pública
resources.what: A free suicide prevention line, open 24 hours across the country and answered by trained staff. It supports people in distress and people who want to help someone else.

resources.name: Línea Azul
resources.org: Instituto del Niño y Adolescente del Uruguay (INAU)
resources.what: INAU's free line to report that a child or teenager is being mistreated, abused or neglected. Reports are anonymous.
resources.how: Call 0800 5050 from any phone, or *5050 from a mobile: Monday to Friday 8am to 8pm, weekends 9am to 7pm, working holidays 10am to 4pm. It is not an emergency service: in danger right now, call 911.

resources.name: Asignación Familiar – Plan de Equidad
resources.what: A payment for children and teenagers, pregnant women and disabled people in households in socioeconomic vulnerability. Children up to 5 need a health card, and from 5 a school certificate.
resources.how: Apply in person at the BPS office in your department, with the ID cards of everyone in your household; if you are pregnant, bring your obstetric card. Questions: BPS on 0800 1997 (*1997 from a mobile), Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm, or MIDES on 0800 7263, Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm.

emergency.label: Police. For a medical emergency, call 115; for fire and rescue, 114

resources.name: Tổng đài quốc gia 117
resources.org: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism
resources.what: The national hotline for domestic violence, open 24/7 across the country. Operators take reports, give first counselling, check your safety straight away and connect you with local help: health care, safe houses, legal aid, or the police and commune authorities when it is urgent. Calls about children, pregnant women, disabled and older people come first.
resources.how: Call or text 117. In danger right now, call 113.

resources.name: Tổng đài quốc gia bảo vệ trẻ em 111
resources.org: Department of Maternal and Child Health, Ministry of Health
resources.what: The national child protection line, free and open 24/7. It takes reports of child abuse and risk, and gives psychological and legal advice to children, parents and carers.
resources.how: Call 111, or use the 111 app or Zalo ('Tổng đài 111').

resources.name: Chế độ thai sản (maternity benefit)
resources.what: Mothers with compulsory social insurance get 6 months of leave for the birth, paid leave for up to five prenatal check-ups, and a one-off allowance of twice the reference level for each child. For a second child, leave is 7 months under the rule in force from 1 July 2026, if you meet its conditions. With voluntary social insurance, the allowance is 2,000,000 đồng for each child.
resources.how: You usually need social insurance contributions for at least 6 of the 12 months before the birth. Ask your employer or your social insurance office how to claim.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: Lifeline 933
resources.what: A free line for adults, open day and night, for gender-based violence, mental health worries and other hard times. Counsellors listen and refer you on for help.
resources.how: Call 933 for free. Texting and online counselling are offered too.

resources.name: Childline 116
resources.what: A free line for children, open day and night, in English and seven Zambian languages. It helps with abuse, neglect, child marriage, bullying and more.
resources.how: Dial 116 for free.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance from an Econet phone. On NetOne, dial 114

resources.name: Musasa helpline
resources.what: A free line, open any hour, for women and girls facing violence at home or sexual violence. Musasa offers counselling, safe shelter, and help getting medical care quickly after rape.
resources.how: Call 08080074 from Econet or 08010074 from NetOne.

resources.name: Childline 116
resources.what: A free line for children up to 18, open day and night from any network. Adults can contact Childline to report a child being abused.
resources.how: Dial 116. You can also send a WhatsApp to +263 719 116 116.
